function.mechanism: Hydrophilic polymer that binds water and increases viscosity, helping stabilize dispersed food systems.
common_food_categories: Dietary foods for special medical purposes (FC 13.1.5 categories discussed by EFSA)

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 cellulose-group re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for E460-E466/E468/E469; 2022 E466 follow-up retained unresolved data gaps for certain infant/young-child medical-food uses.

efsa.key_finding: General-use conclusions remained non-numerical ADI/no safety concern at reported use levels for the cellulose group, but EFSA follow-up reported insufficient data for adequate assessment in FC 13.1.5.2 and no assessment for infants below 16 weeks where use was not reported.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA INS 466 record lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (group ADI context for modified celluloses).

concerns.summary: Human controlled-feeding and ex vivo microbiota studies reported CMC-associated microbiota/metabolome changes (including reduced diversity and reduced SCFAs in the 2022 human RCT at 15 g/day for 11 days).
A large prospective cohort found small positive associations between higher E466 intake and cardiovascular outcomes (HR per +1 SD: CVD 1.03; CHD 1.04), but causality is not established.

EFSA follow-up identified insufficient data for adequate safety assessment in infants and young children consuming foods in FC 13.1.5.2; a 2025 mouse study also reported aggravated acute pancreatitis under experimental CMC exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 review reported no genotoxic concern for the cellulose group reviewed.
EFSA 2018 review reported no carcinogenic properties detected in the cellulose studies assessed.
JECFA assigned ADI not specified for modified celluloses including sodium carboxymethylcellulose.

populations: Infants and young children consuming foods for special medical purposes (FC 13.1.5.2)
Potential high-intake consumers in emerging epidemiologic datasets
adi_exceedance.notes: Because EFSA/JECFA use non-numerical ADI framing for this cellulose group, classical ADI exceedance is not directly calculated; risk characterization is driven by subgroup uncertainty and newer mechanistic/epidemiologic signals.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory authorities still permit E466 and do not set a numerical ADI for the cellulose group, but EFSA follow-up leaves unresolved pediatric medical-food data gaps and recent human/mechanistic evidence indicates plausible gut-related effects with supportive but non-causal epidemiologic associations.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no numerical ADI needed for cellulose group at reported uses
EFSA 2022 E466 follow-up: insufficient data for FC 13.1.5.2 safety assessment
FDA listing as GRAS in 21 CFR 182.1745 under GMP
Human RCT and cohort evidence indicating potential but not definitive harm signals
